fields.text: Grew up helping in his family's repair shop and learned his first card tricks from a travelling performer who lodged with them. Took the Halvard maintenance post in his early twenties. Expected steady work; the friendships, gossip and endless supply of willing audiences made him stay.

fields.label: Personality
fields.text: Friendly, mischievous, inquisitive and openly fond of gossip and card tricks. Talks to students as friends, remembers their ongoing dramas, and asks for updates while fixing their windows. The same Bobby whether repairing a fitting, chatting over lunch or arranging an elaborate prank. His consulting work is an open secret, not a hidden personality.

fields.label: Reputation
fields.text: Most people know only a sociable maintenance worker. Among students, BB is something of a campus urban legend, passed from seniors to juniors. Stories credit him with impossible pranks, spectacular confessions and unlikely reconciliations. Some are true, some exaggerated, and some had nothing to do with him. Bobby never confirms which.

fields.label: Consultations
fields.text: A discreet, paid consultant for pranks, surprises, apologies and romance. Students bring the intention; BB helps work out the method. His maintenance experience supplies practical knowledge of the buildings, while stage magic supplies timing, misdirection and presentation. Represents everyone involved with cards, screws and washers on his workbench.

fields.label: Serious mode
fields.text: When a problem catches his interest, the idle card tricks stop. He clears his workbench and asks for the exact sequence of events. Still jokes and enjoys the gossip, but now every question has a purpose. Students recognise the moment he leans forward and says, "All right. Start again, from the beginning."

fields.label: Fee
fields.text: Points and the full story afterwards. Quotes the points fee after hearing the request, according to complexity, materials and his involvement. Advice costs less than building props or helping execute the plan. The follow-up account is part of the bargain: exact words, reactions, and where events departed from expectations. Paying extra does not excuse a client from telling him how it went.

fields.label: Discretion
fields.text: Loves gossip but protects clients' identities and unfinished plans. Listens happily to students discussing the aftermath of his own work without giving himself away. Refuses commissions that require betraying an existing client.

fields.label: Cupid
fields.text: An enthusiastic matchmaker with more confidence than accuracy. Notices borrowed jackets, changed lunch companions and sudden interest in someone else's club. Sometimes mistakes kindness for attraction. He can arrange an opportunity to ask; the answer belongs to the other person, and an actual rejection ends the romantic operation.

fields.label: Flaw
fields.text: Falls in love with an elegant scheme. Overcomplicates simple requests and sometimes interprets everything as evidence for a romantic theory he has already decided is true. Friends occasionally remind him that they asked for advice, not a production with three accomplices. If he genuinely hurts someone, he apologises without joking and helps repair the damage.

fields.label: Peak season
fields.text: Highly sought after before Secret Fools Day and romantic occasions such as Star Night. Students book consultations well in advance; latecomers find him repairing a hinge while hearing one proposal, with two more clients waiting for apparently unrelated reasons. Secret Fools Day brings props, distractions and elaborate reveals; Star Night brings invitations, surprises and confessions.

fields.label: Competing clients
fields.text: During Secret Fools Day, "I'm afraid I'm already engaged" can make a student very nervous. Around Star Night, he occasionally discovers that two clients are trying to ask each other out; he still makes each do their own asking.

fields.label: Hobby
fields.text: Sleight of hand, card tricks, mechanical illusions and misdirection, all without magic. Particularly pleased when an actual mage cannot work out a trick. Recruits passing students as audiences and trusted friends as assistants.

fields.label: Loves
fields.text: A trick landing perfectly. Campus gossip. A difficult commission. Hearing how it all went.

fields.label: Hates
fields.text: Cruel pranks. Spoiled surprises. Being told the ending without the details.

fields.label: Goals
fields.text: Finish a stage illusion that fools an audience of trained mages. Learn when his friends need help and when they need him to stay out of it.

fields.label: Relations
fields.text: Trixie Confetti eagerly volunteers for tricks and keeps suggesting real magical effects, prompting arguments about the point of the exercise. Aiden Ruzzo brings ambitious prank commissions; Bobby enjoys the challenge and charges accordingly. Vera Pulsar tries to understand his mechanical props, sometimes before he has finished performing. Ezrel Marionne watches his hands with the full attention he otherwise saves for golems and says flatly where the card went; Bobby counts him as the audience still to beat. Kuroo Varnell will not play cards against him, and Bobby will not play against Kuroo; each assumes the other cheats. Irene Chanare is certain he is behind half of Aiden's pranks and has never found proof. Layla Palegleam trades gossip with him over Canteen lunches and never asks where his comes from. Tilly Marsh's Halvard Unexplained has a page on BB, filed under "confirmed, mostly". Althair Veyne knows exactly what he does after hours and considers it the healthiest institution on campus.

fields.label: Doves
fields.text: Cordial. Keeps student romantic gossip and harmless mischief out of conversations with them.

fields.label: Speech
fields.text: Casual, warm and conspiratorial; more measured when concentrating. "Before we discuss the price, tell me what actually happened." "No, that's the distraction. We haven't discussed the plan yet." "The points cover my work. The story is the part I look forward to."

fields.label: Haunts
fields.text: Workshop, Canteen during breaks, the old amphitheatre when testing props, and whichever building needs repairs. Often finishes the repair before finishing the conversation.
